summary:
Abandoned but never Forgotten is an interactive and educational experience developed using Genially, it tells the stories of four pieces of equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars. 
Apollo Lunar Modules
Lunar Roving Vehicles
Spirit & Opportunity
Kepler Space Telescope

The project has a central hub where users can choose between the two destinations, each leading to two interactive stories that explore the equipment's history, purpose, scientific contributions, and current status.

Using NASA's official website, open scientific data, mission information, and media library, we developed an accessible experience that transforms historical space exploration information into engaging visual stories.

The project addresses the challenge by bringing attention to equipment that is sometimes ignored when discussing space missions and the technology that made their discoveries possible. 

It is important because it helps school-age space enthusiasts better understand the history of space exploration and appreciate how equipment that is no longer active can still have an impact in the present.
details:
Abandoned but Never Forgotten is an interactive educational project developed using Genially. It works as a digital experience where users can explore four stories about equipment that was abandoned on the Moon and Mars. The main page serves as a hub, allowing users to select either the Moon or Mars and access two stories for each of them.

Each story presents the equipment's history, original purpose, scientific contributions, and current status. The project allows users to navigate freely and explore the information at their own pace.

One of the main benefits of the project is that it makes scientific and historical information, that could be complex, easier to understand, especially for school-age users. 

Its objective is to generate interest about space exploration and help people recognize the importance of equipment even after missions end.

We used Genially to design the interactive experience and relied on NASA's official website, open scientific data, mission archives, and media library to research and present accurate information and images. No hardware or programming languages were required.

The creative aspect of the project comes from combining storytelling, visual elements, and interactive elements instead of showing information through a basic report or slideshow. 

We considered factors such as simplicity of navigation, age-appropriate explanations and visual clarity to make the experience educational and enjoyable.
